title: 7 best Xpence alternatives in the UAE in 2026
summary: The best Xpence alternative for most UAE businesses is Alaan, followed by Rydoo for reimbursement-heavy teams and for smaller teams that also collect payments.
body_markdown:
Most finance teams don't go looking for Xpence alternatives because the cards stopped working. They go looking because the card was the easy part, and everything after the swipe (the missing receipt, the VAT line nobody extracted, the manual export at month-end) is still landing on someone's desk.


That's usually the moment a prepaid expense card starts to feel like half a system. If that sounds familiar, it's worth looking at[spend management platforms built for UAE finance teams](https://www.alaan.com/products/expense-management) that cover the whole process, from the card to the ledger.


In this guide, we'll cover the seven best Xpence alternatives in the UAE in 2026, with features, pricing, and trade-offs for each.


## What are the best Xpence alternatives in 2026?


The best Xpence alternative for most UAE businesses is Alaan, followed by Rydoo for reimbursement-heavy teams and for smaller teams that also collect payments. Here's the full shortlist:


> Tool Best for


Alaan Corporate cards, expenses, accounting sync, and vendor payments in one UAE platform


Rydoo Receipt-to-reimbursement automation for multi-country teams


Spendesk Reimbursements, approvals, and invoices without paperwork


BILL AP, AR, and spend management under one login


Tipalti Global AP and reimbursements across many currencies


HSBC Virtual Card Large-value supplier payments for existing HSBC clients


Prices are as listed on each vendor's site at the time of writing and exclude VAT.


## 1. Alaan


**Best for:** UAE businesses that want the card, the receipt, the approval, and the accounting entry handled in one place.


**Similar to:** Xpence.


Alaan is a UAE spend management platform that combines Visa corporate cards with expense management, accounting automation, and vendor payments. More than 3,000 businesses across the Middle East use it, and it holds a 4.7 rating on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/alaan/reviews) , where reviewers score it 97% for ease of use.


Where it differs most from Xpence is what happens after the card is used. Here's what that looks like day to day.


### Corporate cards with controls set before the spend


You can[issue physical and virtual Visa cards](https://www.alaan.com/supercard) to employees, then lock each one to specific merchant categories with daily or monthly limits. Cards work anywhere Visa is accepted and support Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay.


On Premium, cards can also lock themselves automatically when someone hasn't met your compliance rules, like the employee who's been "about to upload" three receipts since Tuesday.


### Receipts that don't need chasing


Employees can submit receipts through the app, WhatsApp, or an email inbox, and Alaan sends reminders for anything missing. The[AI receipt scanner](https://www.alaan.com/services/ai-receipt-scanner-expense-management) pulls out the TRN, VAT amount, and merchant details, then flags duplicates and out-of-policy spend.


That matters more than it used to. With the new FTA supplier checks starting on 1 October 2026, having the supplier's details captured against each transaction saves someone a very long afternoon before the VAT return.


### Accounting that syncs without CSV gymnastics


Alaan connects directly to Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Wafeq, Odoo, and ERPNext, with Dynamics 365, NetSuite, and SAP available on Premium. You set accounting rules once and expenses arrive coded, and your external bookkeeper can get their own access.


If you want to go deeper on this part, here's how[Alaan's accounting automation](https://www.alaan.com/products/accounting-automation) handles month-end.


### Cashback that actually shows up


Premium includes[unlimited 2% cashback on international spend](https://www.alaan.com/card-benefits) and up to 1% on domestic spend. For teams running ad budgets on Meta, Google, or Snapchat, this adds up faster than most expect.


[invygo](https://www.alaan.com/customer-stories/invygo) , a Dubai car subscription company, moved its ad and software spend onto Alaan cards and has earned more than AED 150,000 in cashback across seven currencies.


### Vendor and contractor payments


You can[pay international vendors and contractors](https://www.alaan.com/superpay) through Visa Direct with approval workflows and automated invoice extraction. With the[Business Account add-on](https://www.alaan.com/business-banking) , you also get a dedicated IBAN for domestic transfers and AP automation for bills.


### Alaan's pricing


[Alaan has three plans](https://www.alaan.com/pricing) :


- **Starter:** AED 0/month for up to 10 users, with multiple cards, receipt verification, approval workflows, and core accounting integrations.
- **Premium:** AED 499/month (currently with 3 months free), adding unlimited users, cashback, ERP integrations,[Alaan Intelligence AI features](https://www.alaan.com/products/alaan-intelligence) , and a Customer Success Manager.
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing, adding dedicated implementation, custom ERP and API integrations, and multi-entity support.


The Business Account and AP automation add-on costs an extra AED 79/month.


### Pros and cons


✅ Public pricing and a free plan that covers the basics for small teams.


✅ Receipt capture over WhatsApp and email, with AI that extracts TRN and VAT data.


✅ Direct integrations with most accounting tools and ERPs used in the UAE.


✅ Unlimited 2% international cashback on Premium.


✅ Cards, vendor payments, and a business account in one platform.


❌ Cashback and unlimited users start at the Premium plan, so very small teams on Starter won't earn rewards.


❌ The Alaan card is currently only available to employees of UAE businesses, which matters for groups with staff in other countries.


## 2. Rydoo


**Best for:** Companies with employees in several countries who mostly spend their own money and claim it back.


**Similar to:** Spendesk.


Rydoo is an expense management tool built around the receipt-to-reimbursement flow. Its[AI receipt scanner](https://www.rydoo.com/expense/receipt-scanner/) is designed to turn a photo into a submitted expense in about 10 seconds, and it covers tax, per diem, and mileage rules for more than 80 countries.


### Features


- **Smart Audit:** AI checks every expense for errors and policy breaches, though it's only included on the Enterprise plan.
- **Policy rules and approvals:** Set spending rules and up to two approval levels on Pro, with more advanced flows on Enterprise.
- **Card reconciliation:** Pro and above automatically match transactions from Visa, Mastercard, and Amex cards you already hold.
- **Integrations:** QuickBooks and Xero on Pro, with NetSuite, SAP, and Dynamics 365 as add-ons on higher plans.


### Pricing


According to[Rydoo's pricing page](https://www.rydoo.com/pricing/) , Essentials costs $9/user/month and Pro costs $11/user/month, both billed annually and starting at five users. Business (30+ active users) and Enterprise (50+) are custom-priced.


### Pros and cons


✅ Fast, accurate receipt scanning that employees tend to actually use.


✅ Strong multi-country compliance for per diems and mileage.


❌ Rydoo's own cards are an add-on on Pro and only included from the Business plan, so it's a reimbursement tool first and a card platform second.


❌ Per-user pricing gets expensive as headcount grows.


## 3. Spendesk


**Best for:** Teams that want approvals, reimbursements, and supplier invoices handled in one workflow.


**Similar to:** Rydoo.


Spendesk is a spend management platform that brings together spending requests, employee reimbursements, and invoice processing. Its OCR reads receipt details automatically, and employees can submit claims from their phone in seconds.


### Features


- **Real-time expense monitoring:** Finance can see missing receipts and errors as they happen, instead of at month-end.
- **Mobile reimbursements:** Employees photograph a receipt and the claim goes straight into the approval flow.
- **Duplicate invoice detection:** Common mistakes get caught before they reach your books.


### Pricing


[Spendesk uses custom pricing](https://www.spendesk.com/pricing/) , so you'll need a sales call for a quote.


### Pros and cons


✅ Invoice management and accounting integrations in the same tool as expenses.


✅ Good budgeting controls for teams that plan spend by department.


❌ No public pricing, which makes early comparisons harder.


❌ Built primarily for European businesses, so check local card availability and VAT handling for a UAE entity.


## 4. BILL


**Best for:** Businesses whose bigger headache is accounts payable and receivable, with expenses as a side concern.


**Similar to:** Tipalti.


BILL is a financial operations platform covering AP, AR, and spend management under one login, with spend tracking through its Divvy card.


### Features


- **Spend and expense management:** Budgets, card controls, and real-time spend tracking.
- **AP and AR automation:** Bill capture, approvals, payments, and invoicing on one platform.
- **Accounting sync:** Two-way sync with major accounting software on the Team plan and above.


### Pricing


BILL's financial operations plans start at $49/user/month (Essentials), followed by Team at $65 and Corporate at $89, with custom Enterprise pricing.


### Pros and cons


✅ Deep AP and AR automation in one place.


✅ Accessible entry pricing for small finance teams.


❌ Built for the US market, so confirm what's available to a UAE-registered entity before you commit.


❌ Per-user pricing adds up when you include approvers.


## 5. Tipalti


**Best for:** Companies paying suppliers, contractors, and employees across many countries and currencies.


**Similar to:** BILL.


Tipalti is a global finance automation platform focused on payables. It supports payments to 196 countries in more than 120 currencies, with expense management and reimbursements layered on top.


### Features


- **Global payouts:** More than 50 payment methods for suppliers and employees worldwide.
- **Card reconciliation:** Match spend across Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Tipalti's own card.
- **ERP integrations:** NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and QuickBooks, among others.


### Pricing


[Tipalti's pricing](https://tipalti.com/pricing/) starts at $99/month for Select and $199/month for Advanced, with custom pricing for Elevate.


### Pros and cons


✅ Excellent for high-volume, multi-currency supplier payments.


✅ Supplier self-onboarding saves AP a lot of back-and-forth.


❌ More AP platform than expense tool, and priced accordingly.


❌ Setup is heavier than a card-first platform.


## 6. HSBC Virtual Card


**Best for:** Large companies already banking with HSBC that need secure supplier payments.


**Similar to:** Other bank-issued commercial card programs.


HSBC lets businesses generate single-use and multi-use virtual card numbers for paying suppliers through its online portal.


### Features


- **Unique card numbers per transaction:** Reduces fraud exposure on supplier payments.
- **Reconciliation reporting:** Custom data fields to track spend across the organisation.
- **Fraud protection:** Zero-liability protection on each virtual card.


### Pricing


HSBC doesn't publish pricing for its virtual card program, so you'll need to go through the bank's application process.


### Pros and cons


✅ Bank-grade security for large-value payments.


✅ Fits neatly if your treasury already sits with HSBC.


❌ It's a payment tool, not an expense platform, so receipts and approvals still need a separate system.


❌ No public pricing.


## How to choose the right Xpence alternative


Start by counting the steps between a card swipe and a coded entry in your ledger. Every step a person has to do by hand is where time goes, and it's the fastest way we've found to compare tools that all look similar in a demo.


Take one real transaction from last month, say a AED 1,840 software subscription paid in USD, and walk it through each shortlisted tool:


1. **Card spend:** Could you have set a limit and merchant lock on that card before it was used?
2. **Receipt:** How does the invoice get attached, and who chases it if it doesn't?
3. **VAT data:** Does the tool pull the supplier's TRN and VAT amount, or does someone type them in?
4. **Approval:** Does it route to the right approver based on rules you set, or does someone forward a screenshot?
5. **Accounting:** Does it arrive in Xero, NetSuite, or Dynamics 365 already coded, or as a CSV?


A platform that handles all five without a person in the loop is doing the job. If three of them still need someone, you've bought a card with an app attached.


A few other questions narrow things down quickly:


- **Is most of your spend on company cards or employees' own money?** Card-first tools like Alaan suit the former, while Rydoo and Spendesk are built for the latter.
- **Do you pay a lot of suppliers abroad?** Look for built-in international transfers, or consider Tipalti if AP volume is the main job.
- **How much do you spend in foreign currencies?** At AED 300,000 a year of international spend, 2% cashback is AED 6,000 back, roughly the cost of a year on Alaan Premium.
- **Which accounting software do you use?** Check for a direct integration, not a CSV template.


## Summing it up


Xpence does the card part well. The reason most UAE teams look elsewhere is the work that still happens after the card: chasing receipts, pulling VAT details, coding expenses, and paying vendors from a separate system.


If you want all of that in one platform with pricing you can see upfront, Alaan is the strongest Xpence alternative for UAE businesses in 2026. If your main problem is reimbursing employees across several countries, Rydoo or Spendesk may fit better, and if it's high-volume global payables, look at Tipalti.


The quickest way to know is to run one of your own transactions through the five-step test above.[Book a demo with Alaan](https://www.alaan.com/demo) and we'll walk it through with you.


Whichever tool you pick, it helps to know what good expense management looks like before the demos start, and our[guide to modern expense management](https://www.alaan.com/blog/modern-expense-management-guide) covers that. Switching is also a nice excuse to tidy up the rules, so try the[free expense policy builder](https://www.alaan.com/tools/expense-policy-builder) to set limits and approvals before the new cards go out.


## FAQs


**What is the best alternative to Xpence in the UAE?**


For most UAE businesses, Alaan is the best Xpence alternative because it covers corporate cards, receipt capture, approvals, accounting sync, and vendor payments on one platform, with a free Starter plan and public pricing.


**Is there a free alternative to Xpence?**


Yes. Alaan's Starter plan is free for up to 10 users. Paid plans add cashback and more integrations.


**Which Xpence alternative integrates with Xero, Zoho Books, or NetSuite?**


Alaan connects directly to Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Wafeq, Odoo, and ERPNext, with NetSuite, Dynamics 365, and SAP on Premium. Rydoo supports Xero and QuickBooks on Pro, with NetSuite as an add-on on higher plans.


**Do Xpence alternatives help with UAE VAT compliance?**


Some do more than others. Look for tools that extract the supplier's TRN and VAT amount from each receipt, since that data supports input VAT recovery and the FTA's new supplier checks from 1 October 2026.


**How long does it take to switch from Xpence?**


It depends on your team size and accounting setup, but card-first platforms usually take days rather than weeks. The main work is issuing new cards, moving recurring subscriptions across, and connecting your accounting software.
